title: Feelings & support
goal: Notice when a friend is down and comfort them, say sorry and mean it, celebrate good news and offer condolences.
intro:
Friendships are made when something goes wrong, or very right. This unit gives you what people in Bhubaneswar and Cuttack really say when a friend is stressed (**ଟେନସନ୍ ନିଅ ନାହିଁ**), hurt (**ମୁଁ ସେମିତି କହିବାକୁ ଚାହୁଁନଥିଲି**), sulking (**ଅଭିମାନ**), grieving (**ଖବର ଶୁଣି ବହୁତ ଦୁଃଖ ଲାଗିଲା**) or celebrating (**ପାର୍ଟି କେବେ ଦେଉଛ?**).

On the grammar side you'll see how Odia lets feelings *happen to* you (**ମୋତେ କାନ୍ଦ ମାଡ଼ୁଛି** 'I feel like crying'), how to say *while*, *as soon as* and *until* with the **-ବା** form you already know, and the Odia way of owning up: **ମୋ ଭୁଲ ହୋଇଗଲା**, 'a mistake happened (to me)'.

vocab.note: ମନ ଖରାପ / ମନ ଭଲ ନାହିଁ = feeling low, in a bad mood; ମନ ଭଲ ହୋଇଗଲା = (I) cheered up.
ମୋତେ ନିଦ ମାଡ଼ୁଛି 'I'm sleepy'; ନିଦ ହେଲା ନାହିଁ 'I couldn't sleep'.
Noun from କାନ୍ଦିବା (unit 14): ମୋତେ କାନ୍ଦ ମାଡ଼ୁଛି 'I feel like crying'.
Noun from ହସିବା: ମୋତେ ହସ ମାଡ଼ୁଛି 'I can't help laughing'.

vocab.en: to come over (someone) — of sleep, tears, laughter
vocab.note: Always third person, with the person in the dative: ମୋତେ ନିଦ ମାଡ଼ୁଛି, ତାକୁ କାନ୍ଦ ମାଡ଼ିଲା.
ଶାନ୍ତ ହୁଅ 'calm down' (familiar), ଶାନ୍ତ ହୁଅନ୍ତୁ (polite).
ସାହସ ରଖ 'be brave, keep your chin up'.
ଧୈର୍ଯ୍ୟ ଧର 'be patient, hang in there' (lit. hold patience).

vocab.en: trust; someone you can count on
vocab.note: ମୋ ଉପରେ ଭରସା ରଖ 'count on me'; ତୁମେ ହିଁ ମୋର ଭରସା 'you're the one I rely on'.

vocab.en: to handle, cope with, look after
vocab.note: ମୁଁ ସମ୍ଭାଳିନେବି 'I'll manage / I'll handle it'; ନିଜକୁ ସମ୍ଭାଳ 'pull yourself together'.
From English, the everyday word between friends and for small things. With elders or formally: କ୍ଷମା କରନ୍ତୁ or ମୁଁ ଦୁଃଖିତ.
ମୁଁ ଦୁଃଖିତ 'I am sorry' — for messages, work, announcements and elders. Too stiff for a friend.
Lit. 'knowing and hearing'. ମୁଁ ଜାଣିଶୁଣି କରିନି 'I didn't do it on purpose'.
ମୋ ଦୋଷ 'my fault'; ତୁମର କିଛି ଦୋଷ ନାହିଁ 'it's not your fault at all'; ଦୋଷ ଦେବା 'to blame'.
ଅଭିମାନ କରିବା 'to sulk, be hurt (with someone)'. See the culture note.

vocab.en: to win someone round, make up with
vocab.note: ତାକୁ ମନାଅ 'go and make up with him/her'. Not to be confused with ମନା କରିବା 'to refuse' (unit 18).
Lit. break and fall. ସେ ଭାଙ୍ଗିପଡ଼ିଲା / ଭାଙ୍ଗିପଡ଼ିଲେ (respectful).
ପହଞ୍ଚିବା ମାତ୍ରେ 'as soon as (you) arrive'.

vocab.en: while, at the time of (after the -ବା form)
vocab.note: ଖାଇବା ବେଳେ 'while eating'; ଯିବା ବେଳେ 'when leaving, on the way'. Same word as in ସବୁବେଳେ, ବେଳେବେଳେ.
After a time or place: ରାତି ପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ; after ନ + -ବା for 'until …': ସେ ନ ଆସିବା ପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ. In speech ଯାଏ means the same.
From English; ପଦୋନ୍ନତି is the formal Odia word you see in newspapers.
ମୋତେ ଗର୍ବ ଲାଗୁଛି 'I'm proud'. (ଗର୍ବୀ = arrogant, so be careful.)
ତାଙ୍କ ଦେହାନ୍ତ ହୋଇଗଲା 'he/she passed away'. Even softer: ସେ ଚାଲିଗଲେ 'he/she has gone'. ମରିବା 'die' sounds blunt about a person.
ମୋର ସମବେଦନା 'my condolences' — written and said.

phrases.roman: kôṇô hela? sôbu ṭhik ôchhi tô?

phrases.note: To a ତୁ friend: ତୋ ମନ ଖରାପ କାହିଁକି?

phrases.en: If you need anything, just tell me. (familiar)
phrases.note: The future works as a gentle command: କହିବ. Polite: କହିବେ.

phrases.en: Sorry, my mistake. (lit. a mistake happened)
I didn't do it on purpose.
I didn't mean it like that. (lit. I didn't want to say it like that)

phrases.native: ତୁମ ପାଇଁ ମୋତେ ବହୁତ ଗର୍ବ ଲାଗୁଛି।
phrases.roman: tumô paiṃ mote bôhutô gôrbô laguchhi.

phrases.en: So when's the party? (= you owe us a treat)
I was very sad to hear the news.
May God give his/her soul peace.

phrases.note: ନିଜ = oneself, ଯତ୍ନ = care. Polite: ନିଜର ଯତ୍ନ ନେବେ.

grammar.title: Feelings that happen to you: ମୋତେ ଦୁଃଖ ଲାଗୁଛି, ମୋତେ ନିଦ ମାଡ଼ୁଛି
grammar.body:
In unit 5 you said **ମୋତେ ଭୋକ ଲାଗୁଛି** 'I'm hungry' and in unit 14 **ମୋତେ ଲାଗୁଛି** 'it seems to me'. Odia treats most feelings the same way: not as something *you* do but as something that **happens to you**. The person who feels goes in the **dative** (ମୋତେ, ତୋତେ, ତୁମକୁ, ତାକୁ, ତାଙ୍କୁ, ଆପଣଙ୍କୁ), the feeling is the subject, and the verb is always **third person** (ଲାଗୁଛି, ଲାଗିଲା, ଲାଗେ), whoever feels it.

Three verbs do most of the work:

**ଲାଗିବା** 'strike, feel': ଦୁଃଖ ଲାଗିବା 'feel sad', ଖରାପ ଲାଗିବା 'feel bad, be hurt', ଡର ଲାଗିବା 'be scared', ଏକୁଟିଆ ଲାଗିବା 'feel lonely', ଲାଜ ଲାଗିବା 'feel shy, embarrassed', ଗର୍ବ ଲାଗିବା 'feel proud'.
**ମାଡ଼ିବା** 'come over you', for urges that rise up: ନିଦ ମାଡ଼ିବା 'feel sleepy', କାନ୍ଦ ମାଡ଼ିବା 'feel like crying', ହସ ମାଡ଼ିବା 'be unable to stop laughing'.
**ହେବା** 'happen', with the **possessive** ମୋର / ତୁମର: ମୋର ଟେନସନ୍ ହେଉଛି 'I'm stressed', ମୋର ରାଗ ହେଉଛି 'I'm getting angry'. A mood needs no verb at all: ମୋ ମନ ଖରାପ 'I'm feeling low'.

Missing someone uses **ମନେପଡ଼ିବା** (unit 16), with the person missed as subject: ତୁମ କଥା ବହୁତ ମନେପଡ଼ୁଛି 'I really miss you' (lit. your matter keeps coming to mind).

**The cause** comes as a participle in -ଇ (ଖବର **ଶୁଣି** ଦୁଃଖ ଲାଗିଲା 'I was sad to hear the news', ଫିଲ୍ମ **ଦେଖି**) or with -ରେ (ତା କଥା**ରେ** ମୋତେ ଖରାପ ଲାଗିଲା 'what he said hurt me'). 'For someone' is **ପାଇଁ**: ତା ପାଇଁ ମୋତେ ଖରାପ ଲାଗୁଛି 'I feel bad for him'.

**The trap:** never ~~ମୁଁ ଦୁଃଖ ଲାଗୁଛି~~ or ~~ମୁଁ ନିଦ ମାଡ଼ୁଛି~~. But a few feelings are ordinary verbs or adjectives with **ମୁଁ**: ମୁଁ **ଡରିଗଲି** 'I got scared', ମୁଁ **ରାଗିଛି** 'I'm angry' (ରାଗିବା, unit 14), ମୁଁ **ଖୁସି** 'I'm happy', ମୁଁ **ଦୁଃଖିତ** 'I'm sorry'.

examples.en: At the end of the film I felt like crying.

examples.native: କାଲି ପରୀକ୍ଷା, ମୋର ଭାରି ଟେନସନ୍ ହେଉଛି।
examples.roman: kali pôrikhya, morô bhari ṭensôn heuchhi.
examples.en: The exam's tomorrow — I'm really stressed.
I got scared when I saw the dog.

grammar.title: 'While', 'as soon as' and 'until': -ବା ବେଳେ, -ବା ମାତ୍ରେ, ନ -ବା ପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ
grammar.body:
Odia links two actions in time with a word placed **after the -ବା form** of the verb — the dictionary form you already know (ଖାଇବା, ଯିବା, ପହଞ୍ଚିବା). The -ବା form never changes for person; the subject of the clause stays in its normal form (ମୁଁ, ତୁମେ, ସେ).

**While: -ବା ବେଳେ**
ଖାଇବା **ବେଳେ** 'while eating', ଅଫିସ୍ ଯିବା **ବେଳେ** 'on the way to the office'. For something that was *in progress* when something else happened, use the continuous participle **-ଉଥିବା ବେଳେ**: ମୁଁ ରାନ୍ଧୁଥିବା ବେଳେ ସେ ଫୋନ କଲା 'while I was cooking, he phoned'. In speech you can also **double the -ଉ form**: କହୁ କହୁ 'while talking', କଥା ହେଉ ହେଉ 'as we chatted'.

**As soon as: -ବା ମାତ୍ରେ**
ପହଞ୍ଚିବା **ମାତ୍ରେ** ଫୋନ କରିବ 'call as soon as you arrive', ଖବର ଶୁଣିବା **ମାତ୍ରେ** 'the moment (I) heard the news'. A looser 'once / when' is the -ଲେ form from unit 19: ପହଞ୍ଚିଲେ ଫୋନ କରିବ.

**Until: ନ + -ବା + ପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ** (or ଯାଏ)
ତୁମେ **ନ ଆସିବା ପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ** ମୁଁ ଅପେକ୍ଷା କରିବି 'I'll wait until you come' — literally 'up to your not-coming'. The **ନ** is what people normally say, and it does *not* make the English negative. With a time or place, 'until' is simply ପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ / ଯାଏ: ସଞ୍ଜ ପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ, ରାତି ଯାଏ.

**The trap:** these words need the **-ବା** form, not a finite verb: ~~ତୁମେ ଆସିବ ପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ~~, ~~ମୁଁ ଖାଉଛି ବେଳେ~~ → ତୁମେ ନ ଆସିବା ପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ, ମୁଁ ଖାଉଥିବା ବେଳେ.

examples.en: I listen to music on the way to the office.

examples.en: While I was cooking, he/she phoned.

examples.native: ଖବର ପାଇବା ମାତ୍ରେ ସେ ଡାକ୍ତରଖାନା ଗଲା।
examples.roman: khôbôrô paiba matre se ḍaktôrôkhana gôla.
examples.en: As soon as he/she got the news, he/she went to the hospital.

examples.native: ତୁମେ ନ ଆସିବା ପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ ମୁଁ ଏଠି ଅପେକ୍ଷା କରିବି।

examples.en: I'll wait here until you come.
As she was talking, she started to cry.

grammar.title: Owning up: ମୋ ଭୁଲ ହୋଇଗଲା, and accidents with ଯିବା / ଦେବା
grammar.body:
There are two ways to say 'I made a mistake', and the difference is about intention.

**ମୁଁ ଭୁଲ କଲି** 'I made a mistake' — plain and factual: I did it.
**ମୋ ଭୁଲ ହୋଇଗଲା** 'a mistake happened (to me)' — I did it, but I didn't mean to. This is the form people use when they apologise. The same pattern works for lateness: ମୋର ଡେରି ହୋଇଗଲା 'I ended up late'.

Accidents use **compound verbs** (the -ଇ form + a helper):
**-ଇ + ଯିବା** when something just *happens*, with the **thing** as subject: ଫୋନ **ପଡ଼ିଗଲା** 'the phone fell', ଚାବି **ହଜିଗଲା** 'the key got lost', ଗିଲାସ **ଭାଙ୍ଗିଗଲା** 'the glass broke'.
**-ଇ + ଦେବା** when *you* did it and it's done, often regrettably: ମୁଁ **କହିଦେଲି** 'I (went and) said it', ମୁଁ ଗିଲାସ **ଭାଙ୍ଗିଦେଲି** 'I broke the glass'.

A ladder of apologies, light to heavy:
**ସରି / ସରି ରେ** — bumping into someone, being late (friends).
**ମୋ ଭୁଲ ହୋଇଗଲା** — owning up.
**ମୋତେ କ୍ଷମା କରିଦିଅ** — asking forgiveness for something that hurt.
**କ୍ଷମା କରନ୍ତୁ / ମୁଁ ଦୁଃଖିତ** — polite and formal: elders, work, messages.

Add **ମୁଁ ଜାଣିଶୁଣି କରିନି** 'I didn't do it on purpose' or **ମୁଁ ସେମିତି କହିବାକୁ ଚାହୁଁନଥିଲି** 'I didn't mean it like that'. Usual replies: **ଛାଡ଼, କିଛି ହୋଇନି** 'forget it', **ଠିକ୍ ଅଛି**, **ହଉ, ଆଉ ସରି କହିବା ଦରକାର ନାହିଁ** 'OK, enough sorries'.

examples.en: Sorry, I ended up late today.
The glass slipped out of my hand.

examples.native: ସେଦିନ ମୁଁ ଭୁଲ କଲି, ମୁଁ ମାନୁଛି।
examples.roman: sedinô muṃ bhulô kôli, muṃ manuchhi.
examples.en: I made a mistake that day, I admit it.

dialogue.title: Tea and dahibara after bad news
dialogue.setting: Evening at a roadside stall in Saheed Nagar, Bhubaneswar. Ritu notices that her old college friend Subham is unusually quiet. They are close, so they use ତୁ.

lines.speaker: Ritu
lines.native: ଆରେ ଶୁଭମ, ତୁ ଆଜି ଏତେ ଚୁପ୍ କାହିଁକି? କ'ଣ ହେଲା?
lines.roman: are Subhôm, tu aji ete chup kahiṃki? kôṇô hela?
lines.en: Hey Subham, why are you so quiet today? What's up?

lines.speaker: Ritu
lines.native: କିଛି ନାହିଁ କେମିତି? ତୋ ମୁହଁ ଦେଖିଲେ ଜଣାପଡ଼ୁଛି। କହ ନା।
lines.roman: kichhi nahiṃ kemiti? to muhôṃ dekhile jôṇapôṛuchhi. kôhô na.
lines.en: What do you mean, nothing? It's all over your face. Come on, tell me.

lines.speaker: Subham
lines.native: ସେ ଚାକିରିଟା ମିଳିଲା ନାହିଁ। ଆଜି ସକାଳେ ମେଲ୍ ଆସିଲା।
lines.roman: se chakiriṭa miḷila nahiṃ. aji sôkaḷe mel asila.
lines.en: I didn't get that job. The email came this morning.

lines.speaker: Ritu
lines.native: ଓହୋ, ସରି ରେ। ତୁ ତ ଏତେ ପରିଶ୍ରମ କରିଥିଲୁ।
lines.roman: oho, sôri re. tu tô ete pôrisrômô kôrithilu.
lines.en: Oh no, I'm so sorry. And you'd worked so hard for it.

lines.speaker: Subham
lines.native: ଇଣ୍ଟରଭ୍ୟୁ ପରେ ମୁଁ ଭାବିଥିଲି ହୋଇଯିବ। ବୋଉକୁ ବି କହିଦେଇଥିଲି। ଏବେ କ'ଣ କହିବି?
lines.roman: iṇṭôrbhyu pôre muṃ bhabithili hoijibô. bouku bi kôhideithili. ebe kôṇô kôhibi?
lines.en: After the interview I thought I'd got it. I'd even told Mum. What do I tell her now?

lines.speaker: Ritu
lines.native: ଶୁଣ, ଟେନସନ୍ ନେବୁ ନାହିଁ। ଗୋଟିଏ ଚାକିରି ନ ମିଳିଲେ ଦୁନିଆ ଶେଷ ହୋଇଯାଏ ନାହିଁ।
lines.roman: suṇô, ṭensôn nebu nahiṃ. goṭie chakiri nô miḷile dunia sesô hoijae nahiṃ.
lines.en: Listen, don't stress. Missing one job isn't the end of the world.

lines.speaker: Subham
lines.native: କହିବା ସହଜ। ମୋତେ ଭାରି ଲାଜ ଲାଗୁଛି।
lines.roman: kôhiba sôhôjô. mote bhari lajô laguchhi.

culture:
Comfort in Odisha is practical more than wordy. A friend says **ଚିନ୍ତା କର ନାହିଁ, ମୁଁ ଅଛି** and then *does* something: orders tea and dahibara-aludum, drives over on the scooty, sits with you in silence. Close friends of the same age usually switch to **ତୁ**, and add **ରେ** (to anyone) or **ଲୋ** (to a girl or woman) at the end of a sentence for warmth: ସରି ରେ, ଶୁଣ ଲୋ. Between close friends too many thank-yous and sorries sound distant; with elders, teachers and at work, apologise properly (**କ୍ଷମା କରନ୍ତୁ**, **ମୁଁ ଦୁଃଖିତ**), and in Odia homes a younger person who has upset an elder may touch their feet.

**ଅଭିମାନ** is the hurt, silent withdrawal you show only to someone close — a partner, a parent, a best friend — who is expected to notice and coax you out of it (**ମନାଇବା**). It is not quite anger and not quite sulking; Odia songs and films are full of it.

Good news means **sweets**: after exam results, a new job or a promotion you bring rasagola or chhenapoda to the office or the neighbours, and friends will demand **ପାର୍ଟି କେବେ?** Young people mix in English freely: **ଟେନସନ୍**, **ସରି**, **ଥ୍ୟାଙ୍କ୍ସ**, **କଂଗ୍ରାଟସ୍**.

When someone dies, people visit the family, sit quietly and say little — **ଖବର ଶୁଣି ବହୁତ ଦୁଃଖ ଲାଗିଲା** or simply hold a hand. Speak of the dead with respectful forms (**ସେ ଚାଲିଗଲେ**, **ସେ ବହୁତ ଭଲ ଲୋକ ଥିଲେ**). In Hindu families the household keeps simple vegetarian food, no celebrations and often no cooking of fish until the purification rites (**ଶୁଦ୍ଧିକ୍ରିୟା**) around the tenth to twelfth day; don't invite a family in mourning to weddings or festivals in that time. Christian and Muslim families in Cuttack, Berhampur and elsewhere hold prayers in their own way, and the same quiet visit is always welcome.

tip.title: Feelings happen to you: ମୋତେ + feeling + verb
tip.body:
- The person goes in the **dative** (ମୋତେ, ତୁମକୁ, ତାକୁ); the feeling is the subject.
- The verb is always **third person**: ମୋତେ ନିଦ **ମାଡ଼ୁଛି**, ମୋତେ ଖରାପ **ଲାଗିଲା**.
- ଟେନସନ୍ and ରାଗ take **ମୋର … ହେଉଛି**.
- Never ~~ମୁଁ ନିଦ ମାଡ଼ୁଛି~~.
tip.pattern: ମୋତେ + ନିଦ / କାନ୍ଦ / ହସ + ମାଡ଼ୁଛି  ·  ମୋର + ଟେନସନ୍ + ହେଉଛି

tip.title: 'Don't…' for each kind of 'you'
tip.body:
- **ତୁମେ**: imperative + ନାହିଁ — ଚିନ୍ତା **କର ନାହିଁ** (fast: କରନି).
- **ତୁ**: future + ନାହିଁ — ଚିନ୍ତା **କରିବୁ ନାହିଁ**.
- **ଆପଣ**: ଚିନ୍ତା **କରନ୍ତୁ ନାହିଁ**.
- Then reassure: ମୁଁ ଅଛି, ସବୁ ଠିକ୍ ହୋଇଯିବ.

tip.title: ମୋ ଭୁଲ ହୋଇଗଲା vs ମୁଁ ଭୁଲ କଲି
tip.body:
- **ମୋ ଭୁଲ ହୋଇଗଲା** 'a mistake happened' = I didn't mean it: the apology form.
- Things that just happen take **-ଇଗଲା** with the thing as subject: ଫୋନ **ପଡ଼ିଗଲା**, ଚାବି **ହଜିଗଲା**.
- Things you went and did take **-ଇଦେଲି**: **କହିଦେଲି**.
- ସରି for friends; **ମୁଁ ଦୁଃଖିତ** for formal.

tip.title: -ବା ମାତ୍ରେ, -ବା ବେଳେ, ନ -ବା ପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ
tip.body:
- All three come **after the -ବା form**: ଶୁଣିବା **ମାତ୍ରେ** 'as soon as I heard', ଖାଇବା **ବେଳେ** 'while eating'.
- 'Was …ing when' → **-ଉଥିବା ବେଳେ**: ମୁଁ ପଢ଼ୁଥିବା ବେଳେ.
- 'Until' adds **ନ**: ତୁମେ **ନ ଆସିବା ପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ** = until you come (not negative!).
tip.pattern: verb-ବା + ମାତ୍ରେ / ବେଳେ  ·  ନ + verb-ବା + ପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ

sentences.roman: muṃ pôṛhuthiba beḷe se asila.
sentences.en: He came while I was studying.

sentences.native: ମୁଁ ନ ଫେରିବା ପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ ଦୁଆର ଖୋଲ ନାହିଁ।
sentences.roman: muṃ nô pheriba pôrjyôntô duarô kholô nahiṃ.
sentences.en: Don't open the door until I'm back.

sentences.native: ଡାକ୍ତର ନ ଆସିବା ପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ ଏଠି ବସନ୍ତୁ।
sentences.roman: ḍaktôrô nô asiba pôrjyôntô eṭhi bôsôntu.
sentences.en: Please wait here until the doctor comes.

sentences.native: ରାତି ଦଶଟା ପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ ମୁଁ ଅଫିସରେ ଥିଲି।
sentences.roman: rati dôsôṭa pôrjyôntô muṃ ôphisôre thili.
sentences.en: I was at the office until ten at night.

sentences.native: କଥା ହେଉ ହେଉ ରାତି ହୋଇଗଲା।
sentences.roman: kôtha heu heu rati hoigôla.
sentences.en: We chatted and chatted until it got late.

sentences.native: ଭଲ ନ ହେବା ପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ ଅଫିସ୍ ଯାଅ ନାହିଁ। ନିଜର ଯତ୍ନ ନେବ।
sentences.roman: bhôlô nô heba pôrjyôntô ôphis jaô nahiṃ. nijôrô jôtnô nebô.
sentences.en: Don't go to the office until you're better. Take care of yourself.

lessons.title: Celebrating good news

tip.title: Congratulating someone
tip.body:
- Formal and in messages: **ଅଭିନନ୍ଦନ!** Friends say **କଂଗ୍ରାଟସ୍** too.
- Pride happens to you: **ମୋତେ** ଗର୍ବ ଲାଗୁଛି.
- Good news = a treat: friends demand **ପାର୍ଟି କେବେ?** and the lucky one brings sweets.

new: ତୁମ ପାଇଁ ମୋତେ ବହୁତ ଗର୍ବ ଲାଗୁଛି।

sentences.native: ଗୋଟିଏ ଖୁସି ଖବର ଅଛି, ମୋର ଚାକିରି ହୋଇଗଲା!
sentences.roman: goṭie khusi khôbôrô ôchhi, morô chakiri hoigôla!
sentences.en: I've got good news — I got the job!

sentences.native: ଅଭିନନ୍ଦନ! ଏଥର ପାର୍ଟି ଦେବାକୁ ପଡ଼ିବ।
sentences.roman: ôbhinôndônô! ethôrô parṭi debaku pôṛibô.
sentences.en: Congratulations! Now you'll have to throw a party.

sentences.native: ଅପାଙ୍କର ପ୍ରମୋସନ୍ ହୋଇଛି, ଆମେ ସମସ୍ତେ ଖୁସି।
sentences.roman: ôpaṅkôrô prômosôn hoichhi, ame sômôste khusi.
sentences.en: My big sister's been promoted — we're all thrilled.

sentences.native: ସେ ଜିତିଲା, ମୋତେ ଭାରି ଗର୍ବ ଲାଗିଲା।
sentences.roman: se jitila, mote bhari gôrbô lagila.
sentences.en: She won — I felt so proud.

sentences.native: ତୁମ ବାପାଙ୍କୁ ନିଶ୍ଚୟ ଗର୍ବ ଲାଗୁଥିବ।
sentences.roman: tumô bapaṅku nischôyô gôrbô laguthibô.
sentences.en: Your dad must be so proud.

sentences.native: ପାର୍ଟି କେଉଁଠି ଦେବ? ଆମେ ପାଞ୍ଚ ଜଣ ଆସିବୁ।
sentences.roman: parṭi keuṃṭhi debô? ame pañchô jôṇô asibu.
sentences.en: Where's the party? Five of us are coming.

sentences.native: ପ୍ରମୋସନ୍ ପରେ ସେ ଅଫିସକୁ ମିଠା ଆଣିଲେ।
sentences.roman: prômosôn pôre se ôphisôku miṭha aṇile.
sentences.en: After her promotion she brought sweets to the office.

sentences.native: ତୁମ ପରୀକ୍ଷା ଫଳ କେମିତି ହେଲା? କିଛି ଖୁସି ଖବର?
sentences.roman: tumô pôrikhya phôḷô kemiti hela? kichhi khusi khôbôrô?
sentences.en: How did your exam results go? Any good news?

sentences.native: ତୁମକୁ ଦେଖି ମୋତେ ଖୁସି ଲାଗୁଛି।
sentences.roman: tumôku dekhi mote khusi laguchhi.
sentences.en: I'm so happy to see you.

tip.title: Speaking about a death
tip.body:
- Say **ଦେହାନ୍ତ ହୋଇଗଲା** or gently **ଚାଲିଗଲେ** 'has gone' — ମରିବା sounds blunt.
- Always use **respectful** forms for the person: ତାଙ୍କ, ଥିଲେ, ଚାଲିଗଲେ.
- Keep it short: ଖବର ଶୁଣି ବହୁତ ଦୁଃଖ ଲାଗିଲା, then just be there.

sentences.native: ଗତ ସପ୍ତାହରେ ମୋ ଜେଜେବାପାଙ୍କ ଦେହାନ୍ତ ହୋଇଗଲା।
sentences.roman: gôtô sôptahôre mo jejebapaṅkô dehantô hoigôla.
sentences.en: My grandfather passed away last week.

sentences.native: ତୁମ ଜେଜେମାଙ୍କ ଖବର ଶୁଣି ବହୁତ ଦୁଃଖ ଲାଗିଲା।
sentences.roman: tumô jejemaṅkô khôbôrô suṇi bôhutô dukkhô lagila.
sentences.en: I was so sorry to hear about your grandmother.

sentences.native: ଆପଣଙ୍କ ପରିବାରକୁ ମୋର ସମବେଦନା।
sentences.roman: apôṇôṅkô pôribarôku morô sômôbedôna.
sentences.en: My condolences to your family.

sentences.native: ସେ ବହୁତ ଭଲ ଲୋକ ଥିଲେ, ଭଗବାନ ତାଙ୍କ ଆତ୍ମାକୁ ଶାନ୍ତି ଦିଅନ୍ତୁ।
sentences.roman: se bôhutô bhôlô lokô thile, Bhôgôbanô taṅkô atmaku santi diôntu.
sentences.en: He was a wonderful man. May God give his soul peace.

sentences.native: ସେ ଆମକୁ ଛାଡ଼ି ଚାଲିଗଲେ।
sentences.roman: se amôku chhaṛi chaligôle.
sentences.en: He has left us. (= passed away; respectful)

sentences.native: ତାଙ୍କ ଆତ୍ମା ଶାନ୍ତିରେ ରହୁ।
sentences.roman: taṅkô atma santire rôhu.
sentences.en: May his/her soul rest in peace.

sentences.native: ଏ ଦୁଃଖ ସମୟରେ ଆମେ ତୁମ ପାଖରେ ଅଛୁ।
sentences.roman: e dukkhô sômôyôre ame tumô pakhôre ôchhu.
sentences.en: We're with you at this sad time.

sentences.native: ଆପଣ ନିଜକୁ ସମ୍ଭାଳନ୍ତୁ, ଆମେ ଅଛୁ।
sentences.roman: apôṇô nijôku sômbhaḷôntu, ame ôchhu.
sentences.en: Please stay strong — we're here for you.

sentences.native: ମୁଁ ସଞ୍ଜରେ ତୁମ ଘରକୁ ଆସିବି।
sentences.roman: muṃ sôñjôre tumô ghôrôku asibi.
sentences.en: I'll come over to your house this evening.
